text_blocks_mapping.description: Opening paragraph block. 6 lines spanning approximately y=68–225. Full-width text, no bisections. Folio number '86' is above at y~28–58. All lines run from x~60 to x~920. Line 6 is notably shorter, possibly a paragraph-terminal sub-line.

lines.interaction: Paragraph-opening line (@P0). Full-width, 12 dot-separated units. 'or,aiin' contains a comma boundary marker. Opens with 'p'-prefix 'pshdal' — the 'p-' initial is characteristic of Language B paragraph openers. 'fyshey' — 'f' glyph early in the paragraph, relatively rare.

Continuation, full-width, 12 units. 'los,air' has a comma boundary marker. 'qokar' appears twice (units 3 and 5) — repeated root. 'otam' appears twice at line-end — direct reduplication of the terminal token. '-am' suffix twice.

Continuation, 9 units, slightly shorter right margin (~x_max 900). 'okeeey' has a triple-e cluster. 'oteeodail' is a long compound with double-e internal. 'otaiin' and 'otain' close the line — near-reduplications differing only in the terminal '-n' vs '-in'.
Continuation, 11 units. 'sheeey' has a triple-e run. 'am' as a very short 2-glyph terminal isolate — the briefest token on this line. 'y-' prefix on opening token 'ypchesy'.
Continuation, 11 units. 'chcthody' is a dense consonant cluster. 'ar' as a 2-glyph isolate. 'okary' as terminal — 'y' final suffix variant.

Short terminal line — 7 units, x_max ~660, large right-margin gap (~260 units). Marks the close of paragraph block 1. 'araiiin' contains a triple-i cluster — one of the rarest suffix forms. 'ytaiin' appears at both positions 4 and 7 (the terminal), a near-bookending repetition.

text_blocks_mapping.description: Second paragraph block. 11 lines spanning approximately y=254–549. Full-width text throughout, no bisections. This is the densest paragraph block on the folio in terms of token diversity.

lines.interaction: Paragraph-block-2 opener (paragraph mark at left margin). 9 units. 'fchcfhy' is the terminal — a rare double-'f' glyph token, one of the most unusual tokens on this folio. 'kshdy' is a consonant-dense 5-glyph cluster.
Full-width, 11 units. 'tar' and 'otar' in close sequence — shared root. 'ar' as 2-glyph isolate. 'tarcheeg' terminal ends in 'g' — a relatively rare terminal glyph in Language B.

11 units. 'lkaiiin' opens with a triple-i cluster — extremely rare as a line-opener. 'r' is a single-glyph isolate — one of the shortest tokens possible. 'ykal' and 'ykaiin' in close sequence — shared y-prefix root. 'alkam' terminal ends in '-am'.

11 units. Very high density of 'kar'/'okar'/'qokar' family tokens: 'ykar', 'olkal', 'kar', 'qokar' — four occurrences of the 'k-ar' root cluster. 'otam' and 'ytam' close the line — near-reduplications differing only in the o/y prefix.
10 units. 'aiiin' — triple-i as a standalone token (rare). 'taral' opens with 't-' prefix. 'olkam' terminal ends in '-am'.

11 units. 'poraiiidy' — the opening token contains 'aiii' (triple-i embedded in a longer compound), one of the most extended vowel chains on this folio. 'otshs' is a short dense consonant cluster. 'amom' terminal — a double-suffix compound '-am'+'om', very unusual.
11 units. 'aiiin' again as terminal — triple-i suffix, second occurrence on folio. 'cthy' is a short 4-glyph token. 'or' and 'aiin' as consecutive short isolates.

11 units. 'aiiin' (triple-i) as early standalone token — third occurrence on folio. 'al', 'ody', 'ar', 'aiin' are all very short isolates clustered in the middle of this line — a dense sequence of 2–3 glyph units. 'qokeeey' has a triple-e cluster.

12 units. 'ykar' appears twice (positions 1 and 9) — near-bookending. 'ar' appears twice as a 2-glyph isolate. 'eees' — triple-e as a standalone 4-glyph token, unusual. 'chsky' terminal is a short consonant-cluster close.

8 units. 'qoka' is an unusually short qo- token (only 4 glyphs). 'ykalkain' is a long compound fusing 'ykal'+'kain'. 'dalkalytam' is the longest token on this line and one of the longest on the folio — a multi-element compound fusing 'dal'+'kal'+'y'+'tam'.

9 units, slightly shortened right margin (x_max~830), possibly a paragraph-closing sub-line. 'y' appears as a single-glyph isolate between 'ched' and 'taiin' — one of the shortest possible tokens. 'olkam' terminal ends with '-am'. This is likely the close of paragraph block 2.

text_blocks_mapping.description: Third paragraph block. 8 lines spanning approximately y=595–775. Full-width, no bisections. Opens with paragraph mark at line 18.

lines.interaction: Paragraph-block-3 opener. 11 units. 'os' and 'al' and 'ody' are all short isolates clustered mid-line. 'poldaiin' opens with 'pol-' compound prefix. 'tesaiin' — 'te-' initial is less common as a non-qo/non-ot prefix.

9 units. 'ycheeytydaiin' is the longest single token on the entire folio — a complex multi-element fusion: 'ychee'+'yty'+'daiin'. 'oty' appears twice consecutively — direct reduplication of a short token.

10 units. 'ytaiiim' terminal ends in '-iiim' — an extraordinary suffix: triple-i followed by 'm', almost unique in the VMS corpus. 'aiin' appears twice as a standalone. Multiple 'y-' prefix tokens: 'ychor', 'ytaly', 'ykaiin', 'ytar', 'ytaiiim'.
11 units. 'ar' as 2-glyph isolate. 'yteey' appears twice (positions 5 and 9) — exact reduplication of a token within the line. 'qokees' — the 's' terminal on a qo- word is uncommon.
9 units. Three consecutive 'y-' prefix tokens open the line: 'ykaiin', 'ykeey', 'ykal'. 'teodkaiin' is a compound fusing 'teod'+'kaiin'. 'oeey' — a purely vowel-initial token with double-e.
11 units. 'or' and 'aiin' each appear twice as standalone short isolates. 'qokar' and 'chokar' share the 'kar' root. 'ody' as a short 3-glyph terminal.
9 units. 'otaiin' appears twice (positions 7 and 9) — direct terminal reduplication echoing line 20's pattern. 'chckhy' is a dense 5-glyph consonant cluster.

Very short terminal line — 6 units, x_max ~610, right-margin gap ~340 units. Clear paragraph-close marker for block 3. 'ar' as 2-glyph isolate. 'alosheey' is a long compound. 'lkesy' — terminal with 'sy' ending, relatively uncommon.

text_blocks_mapping.description: Fourth and final paragraph block. 14 lines spanning approximately y=843–1000. Includes the unique +Pr terminal locus at line 39. Full-width throughout until the final short runover. No bisections.

lines.interaction: Paragraph-block-4 opener. 11 units. 'aiir' — double-i with 'r' suffix, a minor variant of the more common 'aiin'. 'shody' appears twice (positions 4 and 5) — direct reduplication. 'ocfhdy' — the 'fh' glyph pair is unusual in Language B. 'olpshy' — the 'ps' internal cluster is uncommon.

11 units. 'pchor' and 'ypchor' are near-identical consecutive tokens differing only in the 'y-' prefix — a prefix-variant pair. 'oeees' — triple-e as a standalone vowel-initial token. 'om' as a very short 2-glyph terminal.

11 units. 'o' as a single-glyph isolate — the absolute minimum token length. 'ar' and 'or' as consecutive 2-glyph isolates. 'teodyteytar' is the longest single token on the folio — a complex fusion of 'teod'+'y'+'tey'+'tar' elements. 'qokeeey' has triple-e. 'cr' is an ultra-short 2-glyph consonant isolate.

9 units. 'ysheoar' — a compound with 'sheo' embedded and 'ar' terminal. 'ytchy' is a short 5-glyph 'y-' prefix token. 'tal' and 'tar' close the line — a near-rhyming pair differing only in the final consonant.
9 units. 'olteeeary' terminal contains triple-e embedded in a longer compound — a notable vowel cluster. 'kchol' — 'kch' initial cluster.
10 units. Multiple 'y-' prefix tokens: 'ytchdy', 'ytedy', 'ytain', 'ytody', 'ykeshy' — five in one line, the densest y-prefix concentration on this folio. 'ar' as terminal 2-glyph isolate.
12 units. 'dy' is a very short 2-glyph isolate. 'or' and 'aiin' and 'ol' are all short standalone isolates. 'aiin' appears twice (mid-line and terminal). 'shdy' is a 4-glyph consonant cluster.
9 units. 'ol' as a short 2-glyph isolate. 'olkaiin' and 'olkeedy' share the 'ol-' prefix root. 'qopcheey' — a 'qop-' compound with double-e. 'otam' terminal ends in '-am'.
9 units. 'ol' as 2-glyph isolate. Three consecutive 'y-' prefix tokens: 'ysheedy', 'ychedy', 'ytaiin'. 'otam' and 'aiin' close the line — short suffix-pair.

11 units. 'qo,kchy' — comma boundary marker within a qo- token, indicating uncertain glyph boundary between 'qo' and 'kchy'. 's' as a single-glyph isolate. 'aim' as very short terminal. 'ytair' and 'ytaim' are near-identical consecutive tokens — a minimal-pair reduplication.
9 units. 'otoloty' is a compound fusing 'otol'+'oty'. 'shody', 'chody', 'ytody' form a near-rhyme cluster sharing the '-ody' suffix root. 'dam' terminal ends in '-am'.
8 units. Two comma-marked tokens: 'cheo,dy' and 'ol,keeody' — both have uncertain glyph boundaries. 'ol' as 2-glyph isolate. 'oreeeg' terminal ends in 'g' — rare terminal glyph.

8 units. 's,ol' — comma marker on a very short 2-glyph token, splitting 's' from 'ol'. Four 'y-' prefix tokens: 'ykeeshy', 'ytchey', 'ykar', 'ytaiin'. This line has a notably high y-prefix density given its brevity.

UNIQUE TYPE: +Pr (paragraph runover/right-aligned or indented final line). Very short — 5 units, and notably the x_min is shifted rightward to ~300, not beginning at the left margin. This is the closing runover line of the entire folio — the final partial line of the last paragraph, set in from the left. 'dy' as a very short 2-glyph terminal close. The large left-side empty space (x:60–300) and the right-side empty space (x:680–920) together mark this as a deliberately indented closing fragment.

isolated_zones.description: Four lines on f86v5 have significantly shortened right margins, marking paragraph and stanza closes: f86v5.6 (x_max~660, gap~260), f86v5.17 (x_max~830, gap~90 — minor), f86v5.25 (x_max~610, gap~340, largest paragraph-close gap in blocks 1–3), and f86v5.39 (+Pr, x_min~300, both left and right gaps — the terminal runover). The +Pr of line 39 is the most structurally distinctive: it is the only line on the folio with a shifted left margin, confirming a deliberate runover/indented close.

The left gutter shadow (x:0–60) is text-free. All text begins at x_min~60 except the +Pr line 39 which begins at x_min~300. The gutter darkening is a physical artifact of the binding, not a deliberate scribal margin.
